newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life to meet sales staff individually.
newsitem.headline: Irish Life to meet sales staff individually.

text.p: Irish Life Plc that it would meet each member of its sales force next week and ask them to reconsider their rejection of Labour Court proposals aimed at settling a 15-month old dispute over its sale structure.

"We will be meeting each member of staff individually on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday and asking them to accept our proposals," William Holmes, general manager of the sales force, told Irish state radio on Thursday.
"We would ask them individually to reconsider their position because we are facing into an abyss, I believe."
The staff, most of whom are represented by the Manufacturing Science Finance Union (MSF), voted by almost four to one against the Labour Court recommendations on Wednesday.
The company, which intends to implement the recommendations on Monday, said it would suspend without pay staff who refuse to co-operate with the new arrangements.

Holmes said Irish Life wanted to introduce new work practises that were standard in most industries and wanted to introduce a new sales process to ensure that Irish Life had the right products to suit customers.
"There is no doubt customers have been unhappy with us as an industry and we want to ensure that we provide every customer with the best quality of advice.
"That means spending some more time with the customer but we believe that will have big spin-offs in terms of extra business and satisfied customers," he said.

But John Tierney, MSF national secretary, said his members had little trust that the current management would implement changes in a fair and even manner, while the Labour Court recommendation compensated only 30 percent of his members.
"There are 70 percent of staff who will be going into a different selling structure and will incur a financial loss as a result," he told Irish radio.
He said the company was looking for too much change too quickly.

"I think the company needs to address the concerns of the 70 percent of staff who are going into a new sales structure. They will be getting less sales support. It will be a different type of selling which will take longer and they need to be compensated for that," he said.
Tierney said the union was willing to continue to talk and meet with the company.
The Irish Life field sales staff numbers 440, of whom 330 are represented by MSF.
